title: The Cipher Writer
covers: how to translate words into an algebraic expression with a variable, coefficients and constants, and how to evaluate it by substituting a value
cert: writing algebraic expressions from words and evaluating them

intro.caption: Lesson 6-5 — writing and evaluating algebraic expressions. Tonight is the academy's training heist: Vale's squad locked their flag in a vault. The keypad takes a code written as an expression, and only Ivy can write it.

balloons.t: The clue says: the code is 7 less than twice n. n is the number of guards.
Step on a laser and we all do push-ups. Gecko push-ups are tiny, but still.
Easy. 7 comes first, so it's 7 − 2n. That's classified.

pages.caption: "7 less than twice n" means start with twice n, then take 7 away. The words say 7 first, but the subtraction goes the other way: 2n − 7.

balloons.t: Name the variable first. Then words become symbols.
My counter says there are 9 guards. Substitute 9 for n and the keypad wants the value.
2n means 2 times n. It does not mean twenty-something.
I left you some backup codes. Some are even right. Good luck.
I'll fix them. I know "less than" now. Sort of.
Three locks left. Your squad can't even write the code.
Zero alarms. Zero push-ups. One very quiet Vale.

win.caption: Name the variable, turn each phrase into an operation, and watch the order: "7 less than twice n" is 2n − 7. To evaluate, substitute the value for the variable and follow the order of operations.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Translate the Clue
gates.prompt: The clue: the code is 7 less than twice n, where n is the number of guards. Write it as an algebraic expression.
hints: Conceptual: "less than" takes an amount away FROM something. "7 less than a number" means the number comes first, then − 7.
Procedural: "twice n" is 2 × n, written 2n. Now take 7 away from that.

steps: Practice clue: "3 less than a number p."
Start with the number p. "3 less than" takes 3 away from p.
So the expression is p − 3, not 3 − p. Check with p = 10: 10 − 3 = 7, which is 3 less than 10.

items.q: Which expression means 7 less than twice n?

options.fb: That is Teo's code. It takes twice n away from 7. "7 less than" takes 7 away from twice n.
That takes 7 from n BEFORE doubling. The clue doubles n first, then takes 7 away.
"Twice" means 2 times n, not 2 more than n.

items.q: Backup clue: 5 more than the product of 4 and k. Which expression matches?

options.fb: The product is 4 times k. You multiplied k by 5 instead.
That adds 5 before multiplying. The clue finds the product first, then adds 5.
"More than" means add. Nothing is taken away here.

gates.pass: Ivy writes 2n − 7. The coefficient is 2, the constant is 7, and the keypad stops screaming.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Plug In the Guards
gates.prompt: Ozzie counts 9 guards. Substitute n = 9 into 2n − 7 and evaluate. Then crack the side door.
hints: Conceptual: to substitute, replace the variable with the number. 2n means 2 times n, so it becomes 2 × 9.
Procedural: write the expression again with 9 in place of n. Multiply first, then subtract.

items.label: 2n − 7 when n = 9:
items.aria: value of two n minus seven when n is nine

fb.msg: You read 2n as 29, then took 7 away. 2n means 2 × n, so 2 × 9 = 18.
You did 9 − 7 first, then doubled. Multiply 2 × 9 first, then subtract 7.

items.fbDefault: Replace n with 9: 2 × 9 − 7. Multiply, then subtract.

items.label: Side door: 6c + 15 when c = 4:
items.aria: value of six c plus fifteen when c is four

fb.msg: You read 6c as 64. The coefficient 6 multiplies c: 6 × 4 = 24.
You added 4 + 15 first, then multiplied. Multiply 6 × 4 first, then add 15.

gates.pass: 11 for the vault. 39 for the side door. Ozzie's gadget blinks cyan twice.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Fix the Order
gates.prompt: Vale left backup codes on the pad. Find the mistakes and build the right expressions.
hints: Conceptual: with "less than" and "more than," the amount after "than" is where you start.
Procedural: underline the starting amount, write it first, then write the operation and the other number.

steps: Take 2 away from it: 8a − 2. Check with a = 1: 8 − 2 = 6, which is 2 less than 8.

items.q: Vale's pad says "9 less than 3 times w" is 9 − 3w. What is the fix?

options.fb: 9 − 3w takes 3w away from 9. The clue takes 9 away from 3w.
That subtracts before multiplying. Start with 3 times w, then take 9 away.
The coefficient of w is 3, not 9. 3 times w is 3w.

items.q: Tap the cards in order to write 6 less than 5 times x.
items.fb: "6 less than" takes 6 away FROM 5 times x. Build 5x first, then − 6.

gates.pass: 3w − 9 and 5x − 6. Vale's traps are fixed. Teo says, "I knew that." He did not know that.

gates.title: Boss Gate · The Last Lock
gates.prompt: Three locks. Translate the clue, substitute the value, and evaluate. Watch the order every time.
hints: Conceptual: write the expression first, then evaluate it. A wrong expression gives a wrong code even with perfect arithmetic.
Procedural: name the starting amount, write the operation in the right order, replace the variable with the number, then use the order of operations.

steps: Practice lock: "5 less than 4 times r" when r = 6.

items.q: Lock 1 · Which expression means 4 less than the quotient of m and 3?

options.fb: That takes the quotient away from 4. "4 less than" takes 4 away from the quotient.
That subtracts before dividing. Find m ÷ 3 first, then take 4 away.
The quotient of m and 3 is m ÷ 3. The order inside a quotient matters.

items.label: Lock 2 · m ÷ 3 − 4 when m = 27:
items.aria: value of m divided by three minus four when m is twenty seven

fb.msg: You subtracted 27 − 4 first. Divide 27 ÷ 3 first, then subtract 4.

items.label: Lock 3 · 7 less than twice n, when n = 15:
items.aria: value of seven less than twice n when n is fifteen

fb.msg: You did 15 − 7 first, then doubled. Double first: 2 × 15 = 30.
You forgot "twice." That is 15 − 7. Multiply 2 × 15 first.

gates.pass: KA-CHUNK. m ÷ 3 − 4, then 5, then 23. The last lock opens. Vale reads the clue again, slowly.

journal.heading: Lesson 6-5 — what the heist taught us
rows: A variable is a letter for a number that can change. Let n be the number of guards.
"Twice n" is 2n. The 2 is the coefficient. A fixed number like 7 is a constant.
"7 less than twice n" is 2n − 7, not 7 − 2n. With "less than," start with the amount after "than."
Substitute the value, then use the order of operations: 2n − 7 with n = 9 is 2 × 9 − 7 = 11.
journal.quote: "The words say 7 first. The math says 7 last. Trust the math." — Chip

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 6-5 (Write and Evaluate Algebraic Expressions) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: naming a variable, translating phrases into expressions with coefficients and constants, and evaluating by substitution. The trap is reversing "less than": writing 7 − 2n for 7 less than twice n.
standards: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers
